description: Add map resize functionality to the editor allowing terrain sizes of 200, 400, 600, 800, 1000 with proportional resolution scaling
steps: 1. In src/game/TerrainSystem.ts, add a `resize(newSize: number, newResolution: number)` method that: disposes current geometry/mesh, recreates PlaneGeometry with new dimensions, reinitializes heightData/materialMap arrays (filling with zeros/grass), re-adds mesh to scene. Also add a static helper `getResolutionForSize(size: number): number` that maps sizes to resolutions (200->64, 400->96, 600->128, 800->160, 1000->192). Add getters `getSize()` and `getResolution()` to expose current values.

2. In src/editor/MapEditor.ts, add a public method `resizeTerrain(size: number)` that: (a) calculates resolution via TerrainSystem.getResolutionForSize, (b) calls terrainSystem.resize(size, resolution), (c) removes old gridHelper, creates a new GridHelper matching the new size, adds to scene. Add a callback `onTerrainResized?: (size: number) => void` to notify UI. Also add a `getTerrainSize(): number` getter.

3. In src/components/EditorUI.tsx, in the terrain section (where terrain brush controls are rendered), add a 'Map Size' dropdown/button group ABOVE the terrain brush toggle. Show buttons for sizes: 200, 400, 600, 800, 1000. Highlight the currently selected size. Add props: `terrainSize: number` and `onTerrainResize: (size: number) => void`. Style consistently with existing terrain controls.

4. In src/EditorApp.tsx, add state `const [terrainSize, setTerrainSize] = useState(200)`. Wire up the `onTerrainResized` callback from editor to update this state. Create handler `handleTerrainResize` that calls `editorRef.current?.resizeTerrain(size)`. Pass `terrainSize` and `onTerrainResize={handleTerrainResize}` to EditorUI component.
acceptance_criteria: TerrainSystem has a working resize() method that recreates geometry at new dimensions
MapEditor.resizeTerrain() updates both terrain and grid helper
EditorUI shows terrain size selector in the terrain category panel
Selecting a size in the UI resizes the terrain in the 3D scene
Exported map data contains the new size and resolution
PlaytestMode already handles variable sizes via mapData.terrain.size (no changes needed there)
verification: Run `npx tsc --noEmit` in the project directory and confirm zero errors
